answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 28 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the nectar solution is checked at the juniper gate and logged, the knoll audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore forfeits the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 28 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
